title: Asperosaponin VI promotes flap survival through HIF-1alpha/VEGF-associated angiogenesis.
authors: Deng, Jiapeng; Chen, Kai; Yang, Jialong; Wang, An; Wang, Haiwen
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药成分ASA VI通过HIF-1alpha/VEGF通路促进皮瓣存活，属于纯湿实验与转录组分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Skin flap transplantation is a vital procedure in clinical tissue repair and reconstruction; however, postoperative ischemic necrosis remains a challenging complication. Dipsacus asper Wall. is a classic traditional Chinese herb renowned for its ability to strengthen tendons and bones, promote fracture healing, and accelerate soft tissue repair, suggesting its potential value in microcirculation restoration and wound regeneration. This study aims to evaluate the potential of Asperosaponin VI (ASA VI) to improve flap survival, which is a critical concern in reconstructive surgery. METHODOLOGY: RNA-seq of sham and untreated flap tissues was performed to characterize transcriptomic changes associated with ischemic necrosis. These data were then integrated with network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to generate hypotheses on potential targets and pathways of ASA VI. A rat McFarlane flap model was established to systematically evaluate the therapeutic effects of ASA VI across multiple dimensions, including blood flow perfusion, angiogenesis, inflammatory responses, and oxidative stress. In vitro validation was conducted in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD). RESULTS: Transcriptomic analysis revealed that flap ischemic necrosis is closely associated with angiogenesis-related pathways, most notably the HIF-1alpha signaling pathway. ASA VI significantly promoted the survival of rat dorsal random-pattern flaps, enhanced angiogenesis and blood perfusion, and suppressed inflammatory responses. In vitro, ASA VI alleviated oxidative stress injury and increased viability in OGD-induced HUVECs; however, these protective effects were attenuated by HIF-1alpha siRNA. CONCLUSIONS: ASA VI improves random-pattern flap survival and is associated with enhanced HIF-1alpha/VEGF-related angiogenic signaling.
abstract_zh: 背景：皮瓣移植是临床组织修复与重建中的重要手术，但术后缺血性坏死仍是具有挑战性的并发症。续断（Dipsacus asper Wall.）是一种经典中药，以其强筋健骨、促进骨折愈合和加速软组织修复的能力而闻名，提示其在微循环恢复和创面再生中的潜在价值。本研究旨在评估木通皂苷VI（ASA VI）改善皮瓣存活的潜力，这是重建手术中的关键问题。方法：对假手术组和未处理皮瓣组织进行RNA-seq，以表征与缺血性坏死相关的转录组变化。随后，将这些数据与网络药理学、分子对接和分子动力学模拟相结合，生成关于ASA VI潜在靶点和通路的研究假设。建立大鼠McFarlane皮瓣模型，从血流灌注、血管生成、炎症反应和氧化应激等多个维度系统评估ASA VI的治疗效果。在体外，对经历氧糖剥夺（OGD）的人脐静脉内皮细胞（HUVECs）进行验证。结果：转录组分析显示，皮瓣缺血性坏死与血管生成相关通路密切相关，尤其是HIF-1α信号通路。ASA VI显著促进大鼠背部随意型皮瓣的存活，增强血管生成和血流灌注，并抑制炎症反应。在体外，ASA VI减轻了OGD诱导的HUVECs中的氧化应激损伤并提高细胞活力；然而，这些保护效应被HIF-1α siRNA减弱。结论：ASA VI改善随意型皮瓣存活，并与增强HIF-1α/VEGF相关血管生成信号相关。
